Sundhedsklynge Syd is a regional healthcare cluster in Denmark, operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src5]. It is one of the local organizational units monitored in the national quality reports for the treatment of [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation), published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program (RKKP). The cluster's performance is evaluated against national clinical standards to ensure consistent and effective cardiovascular care across the Danish healthcare system.

In the 2024 quality monitoring reports, Sundhedsklynge Syd drew attention for failing to meet the national standard of 90% for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients. The cluster recorded a result of 89.9% [^src1]. Furthermore, the cluster recorded the lowest proportion among all clusters for [[indikator-4a2|Indikator 4a2]] (2-year treatment coverage), achieving only 84.3% (95% CI: 80.6–87.6) [^src2]. 

Beyond anticoagulation coverage, the cluster is also tracked for patient outcomes and monitoring practices. It is included in the geographic distribution mapping of the incidence of stroke (apoplexy) under [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src4]. Additional data tracks the cluster's performance regarding severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis [^src6], heart failure incidence [^src7], and mortality [^src11], highlighting its role in the broader hierarchical quality improvement strategy where regions and clusters identify strengths and weaknesses in their clinical practice.
